evidence: Draft: "What is one next thing I can do?" Words replaced (SOURCE.txt): "Give me one next action!" Meaning to keep (the working copy's request he approved, batch 470): "Prepare me BEFORE you break it open! Ground me BEFORE you show me the memory! Support me BEFORE you make it intense! Give me one next action!" (his published guide: "If the full truth would overwhelm me, please do not reveal it all. Show me the capacity before the content.") the_change says the draft is Emulate's sentence for the approved one; it claims no put-back, and the draft is exactly that sentence, so nothing is owed back. PRESERVATION, word by word: 'one next' is kept; the ask is the same one, a single small next step for the speaker, put to the subconscious that the whole quotation addresses ("Dear Wise Subconscious Mind"). Nothing is added in the way of a claim, person or number. Three differences, none of which changes what is asked, and the card should state them: (1) form and strength: an imperative request with an exclamation mark ('Give me ...!') becomes a question ('What is ...?'), which is softer, and the fourth request no longer shares the 'X me' shape of the three before it; (2) 'action' becomes 'thing I can do': 'I can' adds a sense of what is within my ability, a condition that is not in the approved line, though it is the idiomatic 'a thing I can do' and sits with the section's own 'in a way that you CAN tolerate' and 'capacity over content', so I read it as no real narrowing; (3) the grammatical doer moves from the subconscious ('Give me') to the speaker ('I can do'), but the speaker is still asking the subconscious to supply the step, so who supplies the step and who acts on it is the same. Said aloud to the subconscious it works; a reader could in principle take it as self-talk, but it sits inside the quoted address and after three 'me' requests, so I do not think that is the natural reading. The safety content is untouched: the three BEFORE requests (prepare, ground, support) are unchanged in CONTEXT.txt. TELLS, judged in context against all rows: none is happening. T02/T12: the script's run of requests, including the triad of BEFORE lines, is the unchanged approved text; the draft is its last item and turns the last command into a question, so it adds nothing to the cadence. T20/T29: it is the script's operative ask, a new request and not a restatement or moral, in the place the replaced short imperative held, and the quotation trails off on 'etc.', so it is not a polished closer. T24: the question is put to the subconscious and the text does not answer it. T26: 'Do what you can' earlier in the script and 'I can do' here echo each other (you do what you can; what can I do), a callback with a job and not a stuck phrase. T01/C03: the 'I' is the reader speaking in the script, not Joel. The writer's ledger lines for T14 and T15 ('puts back the author's own point that Emulate dropped'; 'puts back the author's words or meaning') are template wording that does not fit this card, since nothing is put back; the rows themselves are still ABSENT (nothing moved, no rarer synonym swapped in: 'thing I can do' is plainer than 'action'). The other rows are not happening: no filler, image, aftercare, colon, tic word, generic scenery or invented fact; C02 'one next thing' points at the preparation just before it. LINTER: "B7 short landing at paragraph end" accepted: the linter sees the draft alone; in the article it is the last request in a quoted script that closes and goes on 'etc.', and the next paragraph begins 'REMEMBER:'; the sentence it replaces was an equally short last line in the same place, and this one is a request, not a summing-up. "D9 follows the source order" accepted: a one-sentence swap for its own rewrite follows the source's order by construction, and a single request has no organization for T13 or T09 to judge. READS RIGHT in context: after the three BEFORE requests the question asks what to do next, in the same register as the 'Just ask for what you need to know' questions above it.
